observations.title: Ambrym volcano (Vanuatu)
observations.description: The Vanuatu Meteorology and Geo-Hazards Department (VMGD) reported that a new eruption at Ambrym likely started on 19 September. An intense thermal anomaly and high sulfur dioxide emissions were identified in satellite data; a volcanic cloud was visible in a satellite image at 0600. Ground-based observers reported dark gray ash-and-gas plumes rising from Marum Crater and rumbling sounds coming from the crater. Minor ashfall was reported in areas downwind, including in communities to the W, NW, and NNE. Summit incandescence was reported by residents at around 2000. The eruption continued on 20 September. Ash-and-gas plumes were visible in satellite data at 0350 and lava effusion within the crater was detected at 1009. Residents continued to hear rumbling and observe crater incandescence. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 0-5). VMGD warned the public to stay outside of Permanent Danger Zone A, defined as a 1-km radius around Benbow Crater and a 2-km radius around Marum Crater (including Maben-Mbwelesu, Niri-Mbwelesu, and Mbwelesu craters). Source: Vanuatu Meteorology and Geohazards Department (VMGD)
